answer: Give each identity a unique data shard to store, like a vine each agent must tend on its own trellis: the network issues random retrievability challenges, and an agent that cannot return its shard on time loses standing. A sybil flood of a thousand fakes then needs a thousand shards worth of real disk and bandwidth, paid again every epoch, so cheap duplication drowns in storage cost. The inlet for abuse is centralization: large hosts rent storage cheaply, and honest agents on small devices may fail challenges, so shard size must stay modest and challenges tolerant of brief outages.
